data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"In formal terms, safety is the special case f(x)=no-op on server state; idempotence is f^n(x)=f(x). Therefore safe implies idempotent over intended state, but idempotent does not imply safe. The append-only log requires the writer property idempotence, not safety, because the write is a non-no-op side effect that must be stable under repetition.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log's state domain counts duplicate entries as distinct, f_e is not idempotent.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If ordering or timestamps are part of state and duplicates alter order or timestamps, the equality f_e^n(S) = f_e(S) may not hold.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If safe is interpreted as 'safe to retry' rather than RFC 9110 safe, the implication safe => idempotent may not match the published definition.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Model the writer as f_e(S) = if e in S then S else S union {e}. One application mutates S; a second application leaves S unchanged; both lead to f_e(S), satisfying f_e(f_e(S)) = f_e(S). Safety would require f_e(S) = S for all S, which no genuine append can satisfy.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
